title: Tridosha Theory (त्रिदोष सिद्धांत)
content:
Tridosha (त्रिदोष) is the fundamental principle of Ayurveda comprising Vata, Pitta, and Kapha.
- Vata (वात) governs movement, respiration, circulation, and nervous system impulses.
- Pitta (पित्त) governs digestion, metabolism, biochemical transformation, enzymatic action, and body heat.
- Kapha (कफ) governs physical stability, structure, lubrication of joints, tissues, and natural immunity.
Health is a dynamic equilibrium of these three doshas, while imbalance (Doshic Vaishamya) causes disease.

title: Vata Dosha (वात दोष लक्षणे व आहार)
content:
Vata Dosha (वात दोष):
- Qualities (गुणा): Dry (Ruksha), Light (Laghu), Cold (Sheeta), Rough (Khara), Subtle (Sukshma), Mobile (Chala).
- Imbalance Symptoms: Anxiety, insomnia, dry skin, constipation, joint cracking, bloating, fluctuating appetite.
- Diet & Remedies: Warm, freshly cooked, nourishing, unctuous meals (Ghee, sesame oil), sweet, sour, and salty tastes. Avoid dry, cold, and raw foods. Practice Abhyanga (warm oil massage) and maintain regular routine.

title: Pitta Dosha (पित्त दोष लक्षणे व आहार)
content:
Pitta Dosha (पित्त दोष):
- Qualities (गुणा): Hot (Ushna), Sharp (Tikshna), Liquid (Drava), Slightly Oily (Sasneha), Acidic (Amla).
- Imbalance Symptoms: Hyperacidity, burning sensation (Daha), skin inflammation, excessive sweating, loose stools, irritability, headaches.
- Diet & Remedies: Cooling, soothing, sweet, bitter, and astringent foods (Ghee, coconut water, coriander, mint, fennel). Avoid excessively spicy, salty, sour, fried, and fermented foods.

title: Kapha Dosha (कफ दोष लक्षणे व आहार)
content:
Kapha Dosha (कफ दोष):
- Qualities (गुणा): Heavy (Guru), Slow (Manda), Cold (Sheeta), Oily (Snigdha), Smooth (Shlakshna), Dense (Sandra).
- Imbalance Symptoms: Lethargy, excessive sleepiness, sluggish metabolism, mucus congestion, water retention, heaviness.
- Diet & Remedies: Light, warm, dry, pungent, bitter, and astringent foods (Ginger, black pepper, honey, barley, steamed vegetables). Avoid heavy, sweet, cold, oily, and dairy products. Regular vigorous exercise is vital.

title: Prakriti Assessment (प्रकृती विश्लेषण)
content:
Prakriti (प्रकृती) is an individual's unique biological constitution established at the time of conception and remains constant throughout life.
- Vata Prakriti: Slender frame, quick movements, creative, sensitive to cold, light sleeper.
- Pitta Prakriti: Moderate build, sharp intellect, strong appetite, sensitive to heat, ambitious.
- Kapha Prakriti: Strong sturdy build, calm demeanor, deep sleeper, steady memory, high endurance.
Knowing one's Prakriti allows personalized lifestyle and dietary optimization.

title: Vikriti & Imbalance (विकृती व दोष विषमता)
content:
Vikriti (विकृती) represents the current pathological state of doshic imbalance in comparison to the individual's baseline Prakriti.
- When lifestyle, diet, seasons, or stress disturb doshic balance, Vikriti occurs.
- Ayurvedic therapeutic interventions (Ahara, Vihara, Aushadhi, Panchakarma) aim to restore Vikriti back to the original Prakriti state.

title: Agni - Digestive & Metabolic Fire (अग्नी विचार)
content:
Agni (अग्नी) is the digestive and metabolic principle responsible for nutrient absorption, immunity, and vitality.
- Sama Agni (सम अग्नी): Balanced digestion, proper hunger and assimilation (Healthy state).
- Vishama Agni (विषम अग्नी): Irregular digestion associated with Vata imbalance (bloating, gas, irregular hunger).
- Tikshna Agni (तीक्ष्ण अग्नी): Hyperactive, intense digestive fire associated with Pitta (burning, hyperacidity, loose stools).
- Manda Agni (मंद अग्नी): Sluggish, slow digestion associated with Kapha (heaviness, low appetite, Ama formation).

title: Ama & Detoxification (आम व विषनिवारण)
content:
Ama (आम) is toxic, undigested metabolic waste formed when Agni is weak (Mandagni).
- Signs of Ama: White coating on tongue, foul breath, body stiffness, fatigue after meals, heaviness, cloudy urine, sluggish bowel movements.
- Management: Deepana (appetite stimulants like Ginger/Cumin), Pachana (digestive herbs), fasting (Langhana), warm water sips, and Panchakarma therapies.

title: Ayurvedic Dietetics (आहार व पथ्य विचार)
content:
Ayurvedic Dietetics (आहार नियम):
- Eat only when hungry, in a peaceful environment, avoiding overeating (fill 1/2 stomach with food, 1/4 with liquid, leave 1/4 empty for digestion).
- Include Shad Rasa (6 tastes: Sweet, Sour, Salty, Pungent, Bitter, Astringent) in daily diet.
- Seasonal eating (Ritucharya) and compatible food combinations (avoiding Viruddha Ahara like milk with citrus/fish).

title: Doctor Consultations & Panchakarma (वैद्यकीय सल्ला व पंचकर्म)
content:
Ayurvedic Doctor Consultations & Therapies:
- Kayachikitsa (General internal medicine)
- Panchakarma (5-fold detoxification: Vamana, Virechana, Basti, Nasya, Raktamokshana)
- Ayurvedic Dietetics (Customized nutritional planning based on Dosha, Agni, and seasons)
- Yoga & Lifestyle (Pranayama, Asanas, and Dinacharya daily routine guidance)
- Digestive Health (Managing IBS, hyperacidity, GERD, sluggish digestion, and Ama detoxification).

title: Medical Emergency & Red Flag Protocol
content:
EMERGENCY PROTOCOL (आपत्कालीन मार्गदर्शक तत्वे):
For severe acute conditions such as chest pain, shortness of breath, severe trauma, loss of consciousness, uncontrolled bleeding, or sudden paralysis:
Please seek immediate emergency hospital medical care (Dial 112 / 108) rather than relying on an AI assistant.
